messages.text:
"Create a complete, playable martial arts combat strategy game inspired by Martial Arts Brutality.

CORE GAMEPLAY

The game is a tactical turn-based martial arts fighting game combining collectible technique cards, strategic combat decisions and real-time reaction challenges.

COMBAT SYSTEM

- Two fighters face each other in a detailed side-view combat arena.
- Combat alternates between attack and defense phases.
- During the attack phase, the player selects technique cards from their hand.
- Each card represents a different martial arts move, including punches, kicks, blocks, counters, throws, pressure-point strikes and special techniques.
- Executing a technique triggers a directional swipe or timing-based reaction challenge.
- Successful execution determines the attack's accuracy, damage and effectiveness.
- During the opponent's attack phase, the player must react to incoming attacks by swiping in the correct direction or timing a defensive action.
- Allow perfect blocks, dodges, counters and failed defenses.

BODY DAMAGE SYSTEM
Create a detailed anatomical damage system.
Different attacks target different body parts:

- Head
- Neck
- Chest
- Heart
- Abdomen
- Arms
- Legs
- Joints

Damage to specific body parts must have gameplay consequences. Injured arms reduce offensive effectiveness, damaged legs affect mobility, and head or torso damage affects stamina and consciousness.

Include multiple knockout conditions and cinematic finishing animations.

CARD SYSTEM
Create a collectible card system with:

- Basic techniques
- Advanced martial arts techniques
- Defensive techniques
- Counterattacks
- Chi energy abilities
- Rare and legendary forbidden techniques

Each card must have its own artwork, description, energy cost, damage, effects and rarity.

Players can build and customize their own combat decks.

MARTIAL ARTS STYLES
Include distinct fighting styles:

- Shaolin Kung Fu
- Wing Chun
- Shotokan Karate
- Taekwondo
- Muay Thai
- Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu

Each style must have unique techniques, advantages, weaknesses and animations.

PROGRESSION
Create a progression system featuring:

- Experience and character levels
- Unlockable techniques
- Card collection and upgrades
- Character attributes
- Skill trees
- New opponents and increasingly difficult challenges
- Tournament progression
- Rewards and achievements

VISUAL DESIGN
Use a gritty, mature martial arts aesthetic.
Create detailed human fighter models with fluid combat animations, impactful strikes, realistic reactions, dynamic camera effects and dramatic knockout sequences.

The combat interface should clearly display fighter health, stamina, Chi energy, injured body parts, available cards and turn indicators.

GAME MODES
Include:

1. Single-player campaign.
2. Training mode.
3. Survival mode with increasingly difficult opponents.
4. Tournament mode.

IMPORTANT TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Build an actual playable game, not a static mockup.
Implement functional cards, combat calculations, turn management, animations, enemy AI, damage states, victory and defeat conditions.

Start with a fully functional single-player combat experience featuring one playable fighter, one AI opponent, a deck of at least 15 cards, attack and defense phases, and a complete damage system.

Prioritize functional gameplay over visual complexity.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve, join, extname } from 'node:path'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
import { child } from './session-lifecycle.mjs'
import { livePreviewScript, watchProject } from './live-preview.mjs'

export function projectType(root) {
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) {
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)
  if (type === 'vite') {
    const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache')
    mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
    const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies')
    const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json')
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
    let old = ''
    try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {}
    if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) {
      await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root })
      mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
      const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')

  for (const [name, width, height] of [['desktop', 1440, 900], ['mobile', 390, 844]]) {
    const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width, height } }).catch(transient)
    page.setDefaultTimeout(30000)
    const failures = []
    page.on('pageerror', error => { console.error(error.message); failures.push(error.message) })
    page.on('response', response => { if (response.status() >= 400 && new URL(response.url()).origin === new URL(url).origin) failures.push(`HTTP ${response.status()}: ${response.url()}`) })
    const response = await page.goto(url, { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 45000 }).catch(transient)
    if (!response?.ok()) throw Object.assign(new Error(`HTTP ${response?.status()} loading preview`), { exitCode: !response || [408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504].includes(response.status()) ? 75 : 1 })
    await page.locator(process.env.CAPTURE_READY_SELECTOR || 'body').waitFor({ state: 'visible' })
    await page.waitForFunction(() => document.fonts.status === 'loaded')
    const start = await startForCapture(page, {
      enabled: process.env.CAPTURE_AUTO_START !== 'false',
      selector: process.env.CAPTURE_START_SELECTOR || ''
    })
    console.log(`Capture ${name}: auto-start ${start.clicked ? 'clicked' : start.reason}`)
    await page.waitForTimeout(1000)

      if (error.name === 'TimeoutError' || !browser.isConnected()) transient(error)
      throw error
    })
    if (process.env.CAPTURE_STRICT === '1' && failures.length) throw new Error(`Published build failed: ${failures.join('; ')}`)
    await page.close()
  }
} catch (error) { console.error(error); process.exitCode = error.exitCode || 1 }
finally { await browser?.close().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode ||= 75 }) }

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable tactical martial-arts card combat game inspired by Martial Arts Brutality, started from an empty repo, prioritizing functional gameplay over visual complexity.
- Deliver campaign, training, survival, tournament modes; 15+ card deck; attack/defense phases; swipe/timing reactions; anatomical damage; styles; progression; deck builder; enemy AI; victory/defeat conditions.

## Requirements
- Actual playable game, not a mockup: functional cards, combat calculations, turn management, animations, AI, damage states, victory/defeat.
- Start with fully functional single-player fight: one playable fighter, one AI opponent, deck of at least 15 cards, attack and defense phases, complete damage system.
- Six styles: Shaolin Kung Fu, Wing Chun, Shotokan Karate, Taekwondo, Muay Thai, Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu.
- Eight body zones: Head, Neck, Chest, Heart, Abdomen, Arms, Legs, Joints; injuries must affect gameplay.
- Reaction challenges: directional swipe/timing; perfect blocks, dodges, counters, failed defenses.
- Cards with unique artwork, descriptions, Chi cost, damage, effects, rarity; collection/deck building/upgrades.
- Progression: XP/levels, unlocks, attributes, skill tree, campaign/opponents, tournament, rewards/achievements.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; note assumptions briefly when finished.
- Screenshot checks: save small JPEGs, viewport ≤1280px wide, read only the latest.

## Decisions
- Built as a static vanilla ES-module app (`index.html`, `css/style.css`, `js/*.js`) served by the provided default static server; no package.json/build.
- Canvas renderer with procedural side-view skeleton fighters, dojo arena, particles, blood, camera shake/zoom, KO cinematic.
- Procedural SVG card artwork per card (deterministic, no external assets); Google Fonts with fallbacks.
- Combat architecture: `Combat` engine + injected `hooks`; `CombatUI` orchestrates HUD, reactions, animation, results.
- Reaction challenge: required direction + oscillating timing bar; keyboard arrows/space, pointer swipe, tap button, and arrow buttons all supported.
- Save via `localStorage` key `iron-lotus-save-v1`; style selection on first entry; starter collection/deck from selected style.
- Assumed gritty mature aesthetic, fictional techniques, blood effects, and mobile-responsive layout.
- Playwright browser was missing; ran `playwright-cli install-browser chromium` successfully; installed Chromium/headless shell v1243.

## Work State
### Completed
- Repository exploration; confirmed empty static project with default start/capture scripts.
- Created full game data (`js/data.js`): 6 styles, 42 techniques, rarities, body-part effects, achievements, perks, 6 campaign opponents, tournament rounds, survival generators, XP rules.
- Created procedural card art and portraits (`js/art.js`).
- Created procedural audio engine (`js/audio.js`).
- Created canvas arena renderer (`js/render.js`): detailed fighters, idle/attack/hurt/guard/dodge/KO poses, dojo background, particles, camera, health flashes.
- Created combat engine (`js/engine.js`): turns, Chi/Stamina, card play, AI defense/offense, body damage, statuses, counters, KO causes, Last Stand perk, results.
- Created CSS visual system (`css/style.css`) covering menu, HUD, cards, deck/dojo, overlays, reactions, result screen, responsive/mobile.
- Created `index.html` with all screens and HUD structure.
- Created shared DOM helpers (`js/helpers.js`), reaction overlay (`js/reaction.js`), HUD controller (`js/hud.js`), combat orchestrator (`js/combat-ui.js`), non-combat screens (`js/screens.js`), game shell/progression (`js/ui.js`), boot (`js/main.js`).
- Static server running in tmux session `lotus` on port 3000; `curl` returned 200.
- Playwright Chromium installed successfully.

### Active
- First browser render/functional verification has not yet been performed. Next step was opening the page and taking a screenshot after Chromium install.

### Blocked
- None known yet; runtime errors and visual/gameplay issues are expected to surface on first load.

## Next Move
1. Open `http://localhost:3000` with Playwright, resize to 1280×800, screenshot `screenshots/menu.jpg`, inspect latest JPEG.
2. Check browser console/page errors and fix module/import/runtime issues.
3. Complete character creation, enter a campaign fight, screenshot combat HUD/hand, verify arena fighters render.
4. Test card play + reaction overlay + enemy defense phase + end-turn flow via keyboard/pointer; fix turn/animation bugs.
5. Test KO/result/rewards/progression, deck builder, dojo skill tree, and all modes.
6. Test mobile viewport (390×844), save screenshot, fix responsive issues.
7. Verify files, remove unused CSS/JS quirks, and provide final summary with assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/Martial/Martial/index.html`: app skeleton/screens/HUD.
- `/home/runner/work/Martial/Martial/js/ui.js`: game shell, save/progression, navigation, mode setup.
- `/home/runner/work/Martial/Martial/js/engine.js`: combat rules, AI, damage/KO logic.
- `/home/runner/work/Martial/Martial/js/combat-ui.js`: hooks, animation flow, result/reward handling.

# Iron Lotus

A tactical martial-arts card duel built as a zero-build, static web game. Six fighting styles, fifty techniques, eight body zones, and a body that remembers every strike.

![Iron Lotus](screenshots/menu.jpg)

## Play

Serve the repository root with any static file server and open `index.html`.

```bash
npm start        # or: python3 -m http.server 3000
```

No package install or build step is required. The game is plain HTML, CSS and ES modules, and saves progress in `localStorage` under `iron-lotus-save-v1`.

## What is in the game

- **Campaign** — six gatekeepers, each with their own style, AI behaviour and unlockable techniques.
- **Tournament** — four rounds, damage and injuries carry between opponents.
- **Survival** — endless challengers, escalating damage, injuries carried forward.
- **Training** — a non-retaliating dummy for learning ranges, timing and body damage.
- **Six styles** — Shaolin Kung Fu, Wing Chun, Shotokan Karate, Taekwondo, Muay Thai and Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, each with unique passives and starter cards.
- **Fifty techniques** — universal strikes plus style-specific cards with rarity, Chi/Stamina costs, effects, upgrades and procedural artwork.
- **Eight body zones** — Head, Neck, Chest, Heart, Abdomen, Arms, Legs and Joints. Damage to each zone changes combat maths (timing, guard, evasion, stamina, Chi flow) and can produce distinct knockouts.
- **Reaction combat** — directional arrows plus a timing band for attacks and defence. Perfect reads deal extra damage or negate incoming attacks; counter stances punish perfect defence.
- **Progression** — XP, levels, attributes, a nine-node perk tree, Essence, card upgrades, achievements, deck building and unlocks.

## Controls

| Input | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Click / tap a card | Play a technique |
| Arrow keys / swipe | Match the required reaction direction |
| `Space` / tap | Time the reaction inside the band |
| `Enter` | End turn |
| `Esc` | Close the current panel |
| Hover a card | Inspect full details |

## Structure

- `index.html` — screen skeleton and HUD markup
- `css/style.css` — responsive visual system
- `js/data.js` — styles, cards, opponents, perks, achievements
- `js/engine.js` — combat rules, AI, damage, body injury and knockouts
- `js/combat-ui.js` — turn orchestration, reactions, rewards and results
- `js/render.js` — procedural canvas fighters, arena and effects
- `js/art.js` — procedural card and portrait artwork
- `js/screens.js` — campaign, tournament, survival, training, deck and dojo screens

## Notes

- All art and audio are generated at runtime; the only optional network dependency is Google Fonts.
- The game is designed for desktop and mobile browsers (tested at 1280×800 and 390×844).
- Techniques, fighters and styles are fictional interpretations created for this game.

"Create a complete, playable martial arts combat strategy game inspired by Martial Arts Brutality.

CORE GAMEPLAY

The game is a tactical turn-based martial arts fighting game combining collectible technique cards, strategic combat decisions and real-time reaction challenges.

COMBAT SYSTEM

- Two fighters face each other in a detailed side-view combat arena.
- Combat alternates between attack and defense phases.
- During the attack phase, the player selects technique cards from their hand.
- Each card represents a different martial arts move, including punches, kicks, blocks, counters, throws, pressure-point strikes and special techniques.
- Executing a technique triggers a directional swipe or timing-based reaction challenge.
- Successful execution determines the attack's accuracy, damage and effectiveness.
- During the opponent's attack phase, the player must react to incoming attacks by swiping in the correct direction or timing a defensive action.
- Allow perfect blocks, dodges, counters and failed defenses.

BODY DAMAGE SYSTEM
Create a detailed anatomical damage system.
Different attacks target different body parts:

- Head
- Neck
- Chest
- Heart
- Abdomen
- Arms
- Legs
- Joints

Damage to specific body parts must have gameplay consequences. Injured arms reduce offensive effectiveness, damaged legs affect mobility, and head or torso damage affects stamina and consciousness.

Include multiple knockout conditions and cinematic finishing animations.

CARD SYSTEM
Create a collectible card system with:

- Basic techniques
- Advanced martial arts techniques
- Defensive techniques
- Counterattacks
- Chi energy abilities
- Rare and legendary forbidden techniques

Each card must have its own artwork, description, energy cost, damage, effects and rarity.

Players can build and customize their own combat decks.

MARTIAL ARTS STYLES
Include distinct fighting styles:

- Shaolin Kung Fu
- Wing Chun
- Shotokan Karate
- Taekwondo
- Muay Thai
- Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu

Each style must have unique techniques, advantages, weaknesses and animations.

PROGRESSION
Create a progression system featuring:

- Experience and character levels
- Unlockable techniques
- Card collection and upgrades
- Character attributes
- Skill trees
- New opponents and increasingly difficult challenges
- Tournament progression
- Rewards and achievements

VISUAL DESIGN
Use a gritty, mature martial arts aesthetic.
Create detailed human fighter models with fluid combat animations, impactful strikes, realistic reactions, dynamic camera effects and dramatic knockout sequences.

The combat interface should clearly display fighter health, stamina, Chi energy, injured body parts, available cards and turn indicators.

GAME MODES
Include:

1. Single-player campaign.
2. Training mode.
3. Survival mode with increasingly difficult opponents.
4. Tournament mode.

IMPORTANT TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
Build an actual playable game, not a static mockup.
Implement functional cards, combat calculations, turn management, animations, enemy AI, damage states, victory and defeat conditions.

Start with a fully functional single-player combat experience featuring one playable fighter, one AI opponent, a deck of at least 15 cards, attack and defense phases, and a complete damage system.

Prioritize functional gameplay over visual complexity.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"
